ov: More than 20 species of small, mostly nocturnal marsupials from Australia and New Guinea, with long pointed snouts, large ears and strong hind legs. They forage at night for insects and grubs, and the northern brown bandicoot even survives in towns.
rg: Australia and New Guinea, plus nearby islands such as the Bismarck Archipelago, Seram and Halmahera.
df: Insects and grubs, earthworms, spiders, fungi, roots, berries and seeds.
fx: Young spend another 50 to 54 days in the pouch after birth.
The name comes from a Telugu word meaning "pig-rat", first used for an unrelated Indian rat.
